title: Translate incident action items into PRD safety acceptance & rollout checklist
creator: Sofia Patel
background: A recent KV-cache regeneration incident (RCA: cache storms + cascade autoscale delays) produced a set of operational action items. These items were prioritized in the incident postmortem but have not been formalized into product acceptance criteria or rollout guardrails. This ticket converts the postmortem actions into explicit PRD requirements, deployment gating, and testable acceptance criteria so that future deploys include automated safety checks and operator-visible signals.
summary: Create a PRD addendum that encodes incident-derived safety contracts: pre-rollout checks, canary traffic patterns, automated fallback triggers, SLO degradation budgets, and verification steps. Deliverables: PRD addendum, checklist for release engineers, synthetic test scenarios, and a set of tractable acceptance tests that the Console / CI can run before enabling a new runtime or kernel change.
scope: In scope: (1) Convert postmortem action items into acceptance criteria and rollout steps for runtime and autoscale-related changes; (2) Define synthetic canary scenarios and verification metrics; (3) Add operator-visible runbook steps to PRD; (4) Define rollback gates tied to SLO and KV-cache regeneration signals. Out of scope: changing autoscale algorithms or implementing kernel changes — those are owned by engineering follow-up tickets.
out_of_scope: Instrumentation engineering work (new metrics), full autoscaler refactor, long-term capacity purchases — those will be tracked in separate ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Addendum merged into runtime PRD with explicit pre-deploy safety checklist
Checklist includes at least 3 synthetic canary scenarios that reproduce high tail-latency and KV-cache regen load patterns
For each checklist item, define the verification method (synthetic traffic, dashboard query, or CI test) and the owner
Rollback gates: at least two automated gates implemented in the release playbook: (a) p99 latency increase > 2x baseline for 10m, (b) KV-cache regen rate > 5% of active shards for 5m
Define degradation budget phrasing in the PRD: allowable p99 increase and token loss allocation per tenant tier
Documentation: a one-page runbook excerpt and a Console dashboard saved query included in PRD links
success_metrics: New deploys that use the addendum complete canary stage with <2% manual rollback rate (target)
Time-to-detect during synthetic preflight < 5 minutes for defined regressions
Post-deploy incident count related to KV-cache regen reduced by 50% over next two quarters (tracked by incidents tagged 'kvcache')
proposed_solution: Convert postmortem action list into concrete items grouped by phase: preflight (CI/synthetic), canary (traffic shepherding + automated checks), and post-rollout observation (synthetic probes + alerts). Each item will include: metric threshold, verification method, owner, and automatic action (notify / abort / rollback). Use existing synthetic harness (CI-synthetic) to codify scenarios; Console saved queries will be referenced directly in the PRD.
rollout_plan: 1) Draft PRD addendum and checklist (this ticket). 2) Review with ENG reliability & infra, Console, and Solutions (1 week). 3) Create CI jobs for the three synthetic scenarios (ENG follow-up). 4) Ship PRD addendum and require preflight run for runtime-1.22 feature branches for 2 weeks. 5) Monitor canary runs and adjust thresholds; codify rollback gates in release playbook. 6) After 8 weeks, evaluate incident rate and adjust degradation budgets.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic scenarios false-positive (spurious aborts) — Mitigation: run parallel historical-snapshot tests to calibrate thresholds before gating
Risk: Excessively strict rollback gates slow shipping — Mitigation: define temporary 'soft gates' for low-risk releases and require manual approval with operator checklist
Risk: Missing metric coverage for tenant-specific regressions — Mitigation: require at least one tenant-pattern synthetic scenario in the preflight set and add tenant-sampled dashboards to PRD
open_questions: Q1: Which team will own CI implementation of synthetic scenarios? (Reliability suggested; Engineering capacity TBD)
Q2: Should tiered rollback thresholds be tied to Dedicated vs Hosted customers? (pro: reduces customer impact; con: complexity)
Q3: Do we need a new signal for 'KV-cache regen churn' or can we repurpose existing cache_hit/miss and eviction metrics?
